summary:
Veyora Bio – Evidence-Gated Crop Planning Intelligence for Egypt
Veyora Bio is a bilingual (Arabic and English) crop-planning platform designed to help Egyptian farmers make smarter agricultural decisions using NASA climate data and documented crop requirements.
Developed for the "Field Shift – Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge, the platform combines NASA POWER climate information with agricultural data to assess crop suitability based on temperature conditions, water requirements, and planting seasons across Egypt's 27 governorates.
Veyora Bio calculates key agricultural indicators, compares eligible crops, and provides transparent, evidence-based planning insights. Its unique evidence-gating system prevents unsupported recommendations by clearly identifying missing or incomplete information. An optional AI-powered advisor using Gemini helps users understand results in Arabic or English.
By connecting NASA Earth observation data with practical agricultural planning, Veyora Bio aims to support more sustainable farming decisions, improve awareness of climate-related risks, and help Egyptian agriculture adapt to water scarcity, rising temperatures, and changing environmental conditions.
details:
Veyora Bio is a bilingual (Arabic and English) crop-planning dashboard designed to help Egyptian farmers make more informed agricultural decisions based on climate conditions, water availability, and documented crop requirements.

The project addresses the challenges of climate change, water scarcity, rising temperatures, and soil salinity in Egypt. It focuses on helping farmers understand which crops may be suitable for their location and planting season while making the available evidence and its limitations clear.

How Does It Work?

Veyora Bio uses NASA POWER climate data to retrieve daily weather observations, long-term climate information, and historical climate data for 27 Egyptian governorates, as well as custom farm coordinates.

The system processes temperature, rainfall, solar radiation, and soil-wetness data. It combines this information with a bilingual catalogue of 95 Egyptian crops, including 25 priority crop profiles containing documented agricultural information and FAO-56 crop coefficients.

Its decision engine calculates important agricultural indicators, including growing degree days (GDD), reference evapotranspiration (ET0), crop evapotranspiration (ETc), temperature compatibility, and water-supply coverage.

The dashboard compares eligible crops using a two-dimensional Pareto comparison rather than relying on a single overall suitability score. An evidence-gating mechanism ensures that crops are only ranked when the required information is available and properly supported by sources. Missing or incomplete information is clearly marked as "Not Assessed" instead of generating misleading recommendations.

The platform also includes an optional Gemini-powered AI Advisor that explains the assessment results in Arabic or English. The AI advisor cannot modify the decision engine calculations or create suitability scores.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Veyora Bio aims to support more informed and sustainable agricultural planning in Egypt by:

  • Providing location-specific climate information to support crop-planning decisions.
  • Helping farmers understand temperature conditions and crop water requirements.
  • Making agricultural information accessible through an Arabic and English interface.
  • Increasing transparency by showing data sources, evidence quality, and missing information.
  • Supporting better-informed crop selection and future crop rotation planning.
  • Helping farmers and agricultural extension officers understand climate-related agricultural risks.

Our initial pilot focus is the Nile Delta, where irrigation challenges, soil salinity, and climate pressures are particularly important.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed using:

  • Python: Data processing, climate calculations, and decision-engine logic.
  • Pandas: Data handling and analysis.
  • Requests: Retrieving NASA POWER data through its API.
  • Streamlit: Building the interactive dashboard.
  • Plotly: Creating interactive charts and visualizations.
  • Gemini API: Providing AI-generated explanations of assessment results.
  • Docker: Packaging and running the application.
  • GitHub Actions and Ruff: Automated testing, code quality checks, and continuous integration

The main innovation of Veyora Bio is its evidence-gated approach to agricultural recommendations. Instead of presenting a confident-looking score when information is incomplete, the system clearly identifies what is verified, partially assessed, or not assessed.

It also combines NASA climate data, documented crop requirements, transparent water and temperature calculations, and crop-rotation logic in one bilingual platform.

Another creative aspect is the separation between the AI advisor and the decision engine: AI helps explain the results, while the actual calculations and comparisons remain controlled by the system.

Factors Considered and Limitations

Our team considered geographical location, planting season, historical weather conditions, temperature, rainfall, evapotranspiration, crop requirements, irrigation availability, soil salinity, and previous crop history.

We also considered data reliability, source traceability, missing information, and the importance of avoiding unsupported agricultural recommendations.

Veyora Bio is currently a decision-support prototype, not a yield prediction system or a replacement for soil testing and professional agronomist advice. Some crop profiles still require additional verified agricultural information before reliable suitability rankings can be generated.

Future Development

Future improvements include completing and verifying priority crop profiles, integrating additional NASA datasets such as SMAP, GPM IMERG, MODIS, and NEX-GDDP-CMIP6, incorporating measured farm-level soil and irrigation information, and testing the platform with farmers and agricultural experts in the Nile Delta.
